title: Compatibility prober and smoke battery for LTS upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable compatibility prober and a focused smoke+perf battery that runs automatically before any LTS upgrade rollout. The prober will exercise: API compatibility (request/response shapes), KV cache warm paths, continuous-batching behavior, and quantization fallbacks. The smoke battery focuses on fast surface-level checks (startup, model load, basic generation, streaming, function calling) while the perf battery captures representative tail-latency percentiles and cost-per-token estimates for regression gating.

Scope:
- A lightweight prober agent that can target Dedicated and Private clusters (kube jobs + small harness) and the hosted staging fleet.
- A smoke battery composed of ~20 quick scenarios (single-turn/streaming, embeddings, short chat, prefix-cache reuse) that complete in <5 minutes per machine.
- A perf gate run that compares current candidate build against baseline (p95/p99 and median cost metric) and produces a delta report.
- Integration with the Console dashboards and a validation egress: GitHub PR comment + Slack rollout channel summary.

Non-goals:
- Full e2e customer flows or long-running stress tests (these remain in the larger perf-eval suites).
- Replacing existing canary traffic tooling; this is a pre-rollout safety check to catch regressions earlier.
acceptance_criteria: Prober can run against a target cluster via a single CI job and complete within 20 minutes
Smoke battery produces pass/fail per scenario with failure reasons (schema violation, model crash, timeout)
Perf gate computes p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-token deltas and flags >5% regression at p95 as Blocker
Artifacts: generated validation report is posted to the GH PR and a dashboard summarizing runs exists in Console
Run artifacts are stored in S3 with a retention policy and linked from the ticket
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: We chose a small, targeted battery to keep runtime short and actionable. Trade-offs: shorter runs reduce surface area (miss slow regressions) but increase cadence and developer feedback. To limit false positives from noisy hardware, perf gating uses median over 3 repeat runs and compares against a stable baseline tag; this increases run time but reduces flakiness. The prober is designed to be container-agnostic so it can run in-hosted and private environments without requiring privileged access; this simplifies adoption but means some deep system checks are not included here.
implementation_plan: 1) Build prober scaffolding (kube job + small runner) and standardize scenario format (JSON+seed). 2) Implement smoke scenarios (20 quick cases) and perf harness adapter. 3) Integrate results uploader that writes JSON to S3 and posts status to GH PR. 4) Wire Console dashboard ingestion and add a per-build validation widget. 5) Create CI job and add to LTS upgrade pipeline. 6) Run alpha across Dedicated staging cluster and iterate on flakes.
progress_updates: 2026-03-09: Ticket created and initial design doc drafted (Aisha).

2026-03-11: PoC runner that fires a model load and a short generate validated on staging-gpu-2 (Marco). Logs in S3 under s3://redwood-validation/eng-31207/poc/.
2026-03-12: PERF gating prototype implemented; comparing candidate vs baseline uses 3 repeats. Early runs show p95 variance ~3% across machines — added median-of-3 as mitigation.

recent_comments: Mar 12 - Priya (QA): We found a false-positive where a transient network timeout caused a failure; suggest adding retry logic for control-plane calls.
Mar 13 - Jonah (Platform): Suggest adding an env var to force run in 'dry' mode for Private installs so customers can preview checks without uploading artifacts externally.
Mar 14 - Marco (Assignee): Implemented retries and dry-mode flag. Updated PR with configuration docs. Need sign-off from Security for S3 artifact uploads in private installs.
risks_and_mitigation: False positives due to noisy hardware — mitigate with repeat runs and outlier detection
Leaking sensitive data to hosted storage when running against Private clusters — mitigate by adding a dry-mode and optional local artifact sink, and gating uploads behind customer opt-in
Long run times delaying rollouts — mitigate by capping scenario durations and allowing 'fast' vs 'full' batteries
